content: Sulfasalazine is a medication used to manage ulcerative colitis, a type of inflammatory bowel disease. While it does not cure the condition, it helps alleviate symptoms such as fever, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding. After an acute episode is treated, sulfasalazine is also used to prolong the time between attacks. Additionally, delayed-release tablets of sulfasalazine are prescribed for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis. In this context, the medication reduces joint pain, swelling, and stiffness. Early treatment of rheumatoid arthritis with sulfasalazine can help minimize or prevent further joint damage, enabling patients to maintain their daily activities. To use this medication, take it orally after meals with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) as directed by your doctor. To reduce the risk of stomach upset, your doctor may recommend gradually increasing the dosage when starting treatment. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. If you are taking the delayed-release tablets, swallow them whole without crushing, chewing, or breaking them. It is important to drink plenty of fluids during treatment unless otherwise instructed by your doctor. For optimal benefit, take this medication regularly and inform your doctor if your condition does not improve or worsens. Common side effects of sulfasalazine include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, headache, dizziness, or unusual fatigue. The medication may also cause your skin and urine to turn an orange-yellow color. Rarely, delayed-release tablets may appear whole or partially dissolved in your stool. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, in rare cases, sulfasalazine may cause serious allergic reactions (e.g., Stevens-Johnson syndrome), blood disorders (e.g., agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia), liver damage, nerve or muscle problems, and infections. This is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. If you experience any concerning symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before taking sulfasalazine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, sulfa drugs, aspirin, related drugs (e.g., salicylates, NSAIDs like ibuprofen), mesalamine, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Sulfasalazine may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication may increase your sensitivity to sunlight, so limit sun exposure, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Sulfasalazine is chemically similar to aspirin and may temporarily affect male fertility. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Caution is advised if it is used near the expected delivery date, as similar drugs may harm a newborn. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Sulfasalazine may lower folic acid levels, increasing the risk of spinal cord defects. Ensure you are taking adequate folic acid as directed by your doctor. This drug passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Sulfasalazine is very similar to mesalamine and may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., urine normetanephrine levels, liver function tests), potentially causing false results. Inform laboratory personnel and your doctor about your use of this medication. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, regular laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., complete blood count, liver and kidney function tests) should be performed to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for guidance on safe disposal.
